title: Memphis, Tennessee: Understanding Uninsured Hit-and-Run Accidents
metaDescription: Explore the impact of uninsured hit-and-run accidents in Memphis, TN, including statistics, local highways, and recovery options for victims.
excerpt: Educational Memphis, TN guide — 1-year SOL, local hospitals, and insurer tactics. Not legal advice.

sections.heading: Confirm coverage at the scene
paragraphs: Ask for insurance card photos and verify policy status. In Memphis, uninsured motorist rates track with statewide averages — always assume minimum limits until verified.

sections.heading: Your UM/UIM policy in Tennessee
paragraphs: Uninsured/underinsured motorist coverage on your policy may pay when the at-fault driver has no coverage or insufficient 25/50/15 limits.
Notify your carrier promptly; UM claims still require documentation of injuries and damages.

sections.heading: Hit-and-run steps in Memphis
paragraphs: Report hit-and-runs immediately to Memphis police. UM coverage often requires a police report within 24–72 hours.
Seek witnesses and camera footage near Memphis downtown interchange.

sections.heading: Medical and financial documentation
paragraphs: Use Memphis Regional Medical Center if injured. Track lost wages and transportation costs.

sections.heading: When litigation may be necessary
paragraphs: If UM/UIM carriers deny or lowball offers, a licensed Tennessee attorney can evaluate bad-faith and negligence claims against the at-fault driver directly.

sections.heading: Memphis medical resources after a crash
paragraphs: Memphis residents often use Memphis Regional Medical Center, Memphis General Hospital after serious collisions. Level I trauma care is available at Memphis Level I Trauma Center.
Document every provider visit — gaps in treatment are a common reason TN insurers reduce settlement offers.
Keep receipts for prescriptions, imaging (MRI/CT), physical therapy, and medical transport.
list: Photograph visible injuries the same day when safe
Follow discharge instructions and keep all after-visit summaries
Do not sign blanket medical authorizations for the adjuster

sections.heading: Local crash patterns: I-95, I-75, US-1
paragraphs: The metro area sees roughly 8,315 reported crashes annually (est.). High-risk areas include Memphis downtown interchange; Major highway corridor near Memphis.
If your collision occurred near I-95, note mile markers, exit numbers, and direction of travel for the police report.
Tennessee DOT data is available via https://www.tn.gov/tdot.html — useful when disputing fault or road conditions.

sections.heading: Memphis County reports, courts, and evidence
paragraphs: Request the official crash report through the investigating agency. Memphis County Civil Court handles many civil injury filings in the region.
Business security video near Memphis retail corridors is often deleted within 7–30 days — send preservation letters quickly when appropriate.
The Memphis Bar Association offers lawyer-referral resources; WreckMatch LLC can also connect you with independent Tennessee attorneys at no obligation.

sections.heading: Educational disclaimer
paragraphs: WreckMatch LLC is a legal referral service — not a law firm. This Memphis guide is general education only and does not create an attorney-client relationship.
Laws and insurance rules change; verify all deadlines, coverage, and rights with a licensed Tennessee attorney before making decisions about your claim.

sections.heading: Settlement timeline expectations in Memphis
paragraphs: Minor property-damage claims in Memphis may resolve in weeks, but injury claims involving treatment, lost wages, or disputed fault often take months. Insurers may request recorded statements, independent medical exams, and broad medical authorizations — review each request carefully.
Tennessee uses 50% bar comparative negligence with a 1-year statute of limitations for most injury cases. Calendar your deadline from the date of injury.

If you were transported from I-95 to Memphis Regional Medical Center, keep ambulance, ER, and follow-up bills organized. UM/UIM and MedPay endorsements may apply when the other driver is underinsured.
list: Do not accept the first settlement check if treatment is ongoing
Avoid discussing fault on social media
Request adjuster denials or reservations of rights in writing
Compare repair estimates with your insurer's appraisal
Consult a licensed attorney before signing general releases

sections.heading: Document checklist for Memphis claims
paragraphs: Organize a folder (physical or digital) for every document tied to your Memphis crash: police report number, insurance claim numbers, tow and storage receipts, and rental car agreements.
Request itemized medical bills from Memphis Regional Medical Center rather than summary statements — itemized bills help catch billing errors and support future negotiations.
list: Photos of all vehicles and the scene from multiple angles
Employer note for any missed work shifts
Insurance adjuster name, phone, and claim number
Repair estimates from at least two body shops

faq.question: Is this legal advice for my Memphis case?
faq.answer: No. This is general education from WreckMatch LLC, a referral service — not a law firm. Consult a licensed attorney for advice about your situation.

faq.question: What is the statute of limitations in Tennessee?
faq.answer: Most injury claims face a 1-year deadline, but exceptions apply. Verify your dates with counsel.

faq.question: Will my rates increase if I use UM/UIM coverage?
faq.answer: Rules vary by carrier and state. Ask your insurer in writing; using UM after a not-at-fault crash is often protected — verify your policy.

faq.question: Where can I get a crash report in Memphis?
faq.answer: Contact the investigating agency listed on your exchange-of-information form. Memphis County reports may also be available through local police or https://www.tn.gov/tdot.html.
